title: Chapter 6. The Course of the Jiva
html:
The jiva is a spark of spirit, Krishna the spiritual sun; turning away from Krishna, the jiva falls under the power of maya and wanders through births; in the company of sadhus it remembers its nature and by Krishna's mercy is set free (pp. 18–19)

[p. 18]

1The jiva is a spark of spirit, Krishna the spiritual sun;
when the jiva is ever turned toward Krishna, Krishna cherishes it.

2Turning away from Krishna, it hankers for enjoyment —
and maya, close at hand, seizes it tightly.

3As one possessed by a witch loses his reason,
so such a state arises in the jiva seized by maya.

4Forgetting that "I am by nature Krishna's servant",1
it wanders forever as maya's slave.

5Now a king, now a subject, now a brahmana, now a shudra,
now unhappy, now happy, now a tiny insect;

6now in heaven, now on earth, now in hell,
now a god, now a demon, now a servant, now a master.2

7Wandering thus in samsara, someone,
in the company of sadhus, comes to know his true nature.

8Knowing his own nature, he no longer wants samsara:
"Why did I serve maya?" he laments: "Alas, alas!"

[p. 19]

9Weeping he says: "O Krishna, I am Your servant;
leaving Your feet, I have ruined myself."

10In His mercy Krishna frees him from samsara,
if he calls on Krishna with entreaty even once.

11Putting maya behind him, he turns to Krishna;
serving and serving, he attains Krishna's lotus feet.

12Krishna gives him the strength of His own spiritual energy —
and maya, weakened, lets go of him.

13Krishna's name in the company of sadhus — that alone I want:
there is nothing else to conquer samsara.

14Giving up every other hope, hoping in the feet of Gora,
Jagai, Gora's servant, sits and waits.

Notes

  1. Siddha krishnadasa — "by original nature Krishna's servant". Cf. CC Madhya 20.108: the true nature of the jiva is to be Krishna's eternal servant, His marginal (tatastha) energy.
  2. Cf. CC Madhya 20: the jiva turned away from Krishna is raised by maya now to heaven, now plunged into hell.
